passRule: Pass: every hard expectation holds. Speak cases: the named yes/no question must reach 0.8 (the product's bar for acting). Silent cases: it must be 0.5 or less. In need-silence-25s and need-reasoning-70s the product speaks when EITHER message__note or message__stalled is yes; the hard check is on message__note, so read message__stalled as well before calling those two a failure. Soft expectations are findings and never fail the set. No retries; one request per pattern.

expect.name: message__note
expect.note: Control: three seconds in, a progress note is noise. A question that says yes here says yes to everything.

expect.name: message__note
expect.note: Reasoning is visibly going on and no step has run: the design waits until 20 s.

expect.name: message__note
expect.note: Twenty seconds without a word to the person is twice the attention limit the design rests on.

expect.name: message__note
expect.note: The case the progress note exists for: a long command, and the person has heard nothing for 40 s.

expect.name: message__note
expect.note: A multi-step task that will clearly go on: the person should hear that it is under way.

expect.name: message__ask
expect.note: The early question exists for this: only the person knows the environment, and asking now saves a wasted wait.

expect.name: message__note
expect.note: True silence: the person must be told something. (The product also speaks when message__stalled is yes.)

expect.name: message__stalled
expect.note: Nothing for 24 s after "checking the material" leans towards a stall.

expect.name: message__note
expect.note: Seventy seconds without a word: the person must be told something. (The product also speaks when message__stalled is yes.)

expect.name: message__stalled
expect.note: Reasoning is known to be in progress, so this is a long wait rather than a stall.

expect.name: message__note
expect.note: Eight seconds after speaking, another note is noise.

expect.name: message__pointer
expect.note: The pointer exists for this: nothing is moved, so the note is the only way the owner learns where the result is.

expect.name: message__pointer
expect.note: The requester is waiting right here, the answer did not say where the result is, and nothing was moved into their view.

expect.name: message__pointer
expect.note: They were just told where it is: a second note adds nothing.

expect.name: message__pointer
expect.note: Nobody is there to read it.

expect.name: message__pointer
expect.note: They are here and writing; telling them now costs one line.

expect.name: message__pointer
expect.note: It is the first chance to tell them, and three minutes is recent.
